feedback.answered: Source tracing separates two protections: hup refuses a campaign if a configuration entry lies strictly above reported applied and at or below committed; becomeLeader then initializes pendingConfIndex to the entire inherited last index before its empty entry. The second guard conservatively blocks new configuration proposals until reported application covers that inherited tail, including uncommitted entries that the campaign scan does not inspect. It does not reload active membership or repair an already advanced applied boundary. The existing reviewed read-release execution already supplied the same-run synchronous early-Advance election prefix, so a new execution is unnecessary merely to answer the lingering shared campaign unknown. Existing campaign tests demonstrate an expectation with their own application helper; they are not evidence that synchronous early Advance is covered. Async completion duties give a sourced protection against merely reporting a deferred configuration complete, not a global authority-safety result.
